name: Roll from Dead Orchard
description: A Dead Orchard reset opens the high both-arm leg triangle before turning or reorganizing guard. A rolling headlock escape needs a separate starting position.
summary: A Dead Orchard reset releases the high both-arm leg triangle before the bottom player turns or reorganizes guard.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Dead Orchard Control, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Dead Orchard is not an Anaconda front headlock. A rolling headlock escape cannot be taught from this configuration without a separate headlock exchange.

The bottom player faces the opponent and keeps the hips close beneath the shoulders. The legs form a high figure-four around the shoulder line, with both opposing arms inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Nathan Orchard — Dead Orchard, part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoiB1D2WJwE); [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo).

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): What holds the opponent at the start?
flashcards.answer: The starting control is a bottom-player both-arm leg triangle, despite the route's rolling-escape wording.
flashcards.answer_line: Your high triangle around both arms

plausible: Your high triangle around one arm
Your low ankles around their waist
trap: Your high shin before leg closure

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): What must release before you turn or shrimp?
flashcards.answer: Release both arms from the high triangle and remove any wrist leverage before changing hip direction.
flashcards.answer_line: Both arms and any wrist leverage

plausible: Only the hand holding your high shin
One arm with the other elbow fixed
trap: Only leg squeeze; keep wrist tension

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): How do you lower a leg during the released reset?
flashcards.answer: Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle after opening the enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Move the hip with the knee supported

plausible: Pull ankle while knee stays pinned
Turn torso with high legs connected
trap: Lower foot while thigh stays fixed

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): Which movement restores space for an inside knee?
flashcards.answer: After release, a short lateral hip escape behind a frame brings a knee between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: Lateral hip escape behind a frame

plausible: Bridge up with no sideways hip move
Straight-arm shove with hips still
trap: Shift hips; leave near knee behind

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): Which orientation should the reset preserve?
flashcards.answer: The recovery restores facing guard rather than promising a roll into turtle.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulders and hips face the opponent

plausible: Chest turned away with arm trailing
Hips face away; chest toward them
trap: Head toward them; torso faces away

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): What blocks incoming chest pressure as the knee returns?
flashcards.answer: Keep an inside forearm barrier against crossface and chest pressure while the released knee returns.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside forearm on their shoulder

plausible: Both hands following the freed wrist
Forearm outside the approaching arm
trap: Hip frame with shoulder path open

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): Why must both arms be released before a large hip turn?
flashcards.answer: Open the both-arm leg enclosure and release wrist leverage before changing direction. Turning while one shoulder remains caught can load that elbow or shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: Held elbow cannot follow the torso

plausible: Turning frees elbows with legs shut
Free wrists free shoulders too
trap: Loose neck lets trapped arms follow

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (bottom): Why is an Anaconda escape roll not the taught movement here?
flashcards.answer: Dead Orchard is not an Anaconda headlock. Release the leg trap before using framed hip movement to recover guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Leg trap rather than arm headlock

plausible: Both use a neck-first arm thread
Both need one arm outside the loop
trap: Both open by peeling a biceps grip

defender.description: Roll from Dead Orchard (defender): Treat a high leg triangle containing both your arms as an arm-lock threat even when the neck is not being choked. Keep the arms compact and avoid offering a straight arm while trying to force posture.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Dead Orchard Control, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Dead Orchard is not an Anaconda front headlock. A rolling headlock escape cannot be taught from this configuration without a separate headlock exchange.

Treat a high leg triangle containing both your arms as an arm-lock threat even when the neck is not being choked. Keep the arms compact and avoid offering a straight arm while trying to force posture. Maintain an early frame at the hip or thigh before the figure-four closes around the shoulders.

Work on opening the leg enclosure before withdrawing the shoulder and elbow together; stop if an arm is already loaded. Only raise posture after the shoulder line is free; a sudden pull can extend a captured elbow. Use a verbal tap or foot tap if both hands are trapped, and do not rely on pain to judge remaining range.

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (top): What is threatened if you pull a trapped wrist away?
flashcards.answer: Pulling the wrist while the shoulder remains captured can create an elbow-extension lever.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow extension against the leg trap

plausible: Wrist exits before elbow extension
Shoulder clears as wrist moves away
trap: High legs lower as the arm lengthens

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (top): What should you avoid while the bottom player resets?
flashcards.answer: Do not force posture with a long arm inside the high legs; keep the elbows compact during release.

plausible: Keeping the elbows compact
Waiting for shoulder clearance
trap: Using space once the leg trap opens

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (top): Which event closes the early hip-framing window?
flashcards.answer: Use hip or thigh frames before the shoulder-level figure-four closes. Once both shoulders are enclosed, the preventive window has passed; obtain an actual opening before withdrawing the arms.

plausible: First knee nears one shoulder
Hand briefly touches your free wrist
trap: One foot rises before legs connect

flashcards.question: Roll from Dead Orchard (top): When is turning safe enough to resume the positional drill?
flashcards.answer: Resume turning only after the relevant shoulder and elbow are released; a free hand alone is insufficient.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder and elbow free of the legs

plausible: Only the chin feels loose
Partner turns with legs still locked
trap: Hand moves but upper arm stays held
